question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Calcutta — Location & Foundation]
options: Calcutta (Kolkata) is located on the eastern bank of the Hooghly River, a distributary of the Ganges
Calcutta was founded by Job Charnock in 1690 by combining three villages: Sutanuti, Gobindapur, and Kalikata
Fort William was constructed by the English in Calcutta to protect their settlement
Calcutta is situated at the mouth of the Brahmaputra River, providing direct access to the hills of Assam
wrong_fact: Calcutta is NOT situated at the mouth of the Brahmaputra River. It lies on the bank of the Hooghly River in the lower Ganges Delta in West Bengal. The Brahmaputra empties into the Bay of Bengal further east in present-day Bangladesh as part of the Padma/Meghna river system.
explanation: Calcutta is located in West Bengal, India, on the east bank of the Hooghly River (a major distributary of the Ganges), about 150 km upstream from the Bay of Bengal. Job Charnock, an administrator with the English East India Company, is traditionally credited with establishing the settlement in 1690 by leasing the three villages of Sutanuti, Gobindapur, and Kalikata from local landowners under Mughal permission. Fort William was built to safeguard this trading factory. It has no geographical connection to the mouth of the Brahmaputra, which is located in Bangladesh.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Calcutta — Battle of Plassey & Regional Geography]
options: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought on the banks of the Bhagirathi-Hooghly River, north of Calcutta
Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, captured Calcutta in 1756 and temporarily renamed it Alinagar
Plassey is located in the Nadia district of present-day West Bengal
The Battle of Plassey was fought on the high plateaus of the Chota Nagpur region, restricting cavalry movements
wrong_fact: The Battle of Plassey was NOT fought on the Chota Nagpur plateau. It was fought in the flat, alluvial plains of the Ganges delta on the banks of the Bhagirathi-Hooghly River, in the Nadia district of Bengal, approximately 150 km north of Calcutta.
explanation: The Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757) took place at Palashi (Plassey) on the banks of the Bhagirathi River (a branch of the Ganges) in the flat deltaic plains of Bengal (Nadia district). It was not fought in the Chota Nagpur plateau (which lies further west in Jharkhand/western Bengal). Siraj-ud-Daulah had captured Fort William in Calcutta in 1756, briefly renaming the city Alinagar in honour of his grandfather Alivardi Khan, before Robert Clive retook it.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Calcutta — Fort William & Black Hole Incident Location]
options: The 'Black Hole' incident (1756) took place inside the original Fort William, located near the modern General Post Office (GPO) area in Calcutta
The original Fort William was rebuilt and relocated to its present site in the Maidan area after the Battle of Plassey
The French base of Chandernagore was located south of Calcutta, making it a buffer between Calcutta and the Bay of Bengal
The new Fort William built after 1757 was designed as an irregular octagonal star fort with a large open clearing (Maidan) around it to provide a clear line of fire
wrong_fact: Chandernagore was NOT located south of Calcutta. It was located about 35 km north (upstream) of Calcutta on the Hooghly River. Thus, it was situated further inland than Calcutta and did not act as a geographical buffer between Calcutta and the Bay of Bengal (which lies to the south).
explanation: The historical French outpost of Chandernagore (Chandannagar) lies upstream (north) of Calcutta on the Hooghly River. The original Fort William stood in the area of the current General Post Office (GPO) in Calcutta, where the Black Hole tragedy occurred in June 1756. After Clive recaptured Calcutta and defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, the British constructed a new, larger octagonal star fort at its current site in the Maidan, clearing the surrounding forest to ensure an unobstructed line of sight and fire for defence.
